newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks seen higher on rates fall, peso soft.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks seen higher on rates fall, peso soft.

text.p: Traders saw Mexican stocks opening with moderate upside potential following a fall in primary rates the night before, but they expected caution concerning developments on Wall Street.

"Cetes rates fell, much as expected, but I see a slow start as they wait to see which way the Dow goes. We have lagged behind them, and should go up, but people still get nervous," one desk trader said..

Bellwether 28-day Cetes rates fell 134 basis points to 18.37 percent at Tuesday night's primary auction. This compares with an average decline of 115 basis points predicted by traders in a previously conducted Reuters survey.
Traders expected the peso to open weaker due to profit-taking and dollar short-covering carried over from Tuesday's rally.
Dealers predicted a trading range of 7.8900/7.9150 per dollar for the benchmark 48-hour peso. Pre-open bids stood at 7.9010/7.9150 per dollar, compared to Tuesday's close of 7.8960/7.9000.

Overnight rates on Cetes were seen opening close to Tuesday's close of 19.00 percent, even though it was higher than average levels for that session and therre could be pressures from the fall in primary interest rates.
